newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zeitler-likely Germany can meet EMU goal strictly.
newsitem.headline: Zeitler-likely Germany can meet EMU goal strictly.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said on Friday it was likely that Germany would meet the Maastricht deficit goal strictly, and warned against excessive leeway in interpreting the target.
The Maastricht Treaty sets a threshold for deficits of three percent of gross domestic product.

Zeitler told the "Bayerische Steuerzahler" magazine: "It would be the wrong way to deviate from a strict and clear fulfilment of the three percent criterion and open up an upward Richter scale after the decimal point."
The text of the interview was released in advance.
Zeitler has said in the past that EU states should stick by the three percent goal and has also said Germany had a realistic chance of meeting the target this year.
